symbols.name: run_gate
symbols.note: Advisory regression gate comparing current task recall against a stored baseline. Returns dict with pass/fail, regressions, improvements, etc.

claims.text: ADVISORY regression ratchet. Replays ``tasks`` (default TASKS) against a stored baseline.json and flags any PRIMARY-tier task whose recall DECREASED.
claims.why: The code uses baseline_path (default DEFAULT_BASELINE_PATH) and loads baseline.json; iterates over per_task results, skips non-primary and errored/focus_withheld, compares recall for primary tasks, collects regressions where cur_recall < base_recall.

claims.text: Compares PER TASK, never on a mean -- a mean hides one task collapsing while another improves (see tests/test_eval_oracle.py for the mean-preserving-swap test that proves this).
claims.why: The code indeed compares per task (individual recall values), not a mean. However, the reference to tests/test_eval_oracle.py is outside this chunk.

claims.text: Workflow before shipping a slice-heuristic change: python -m daedalus.eval --gate. Expect PASS. A FAIL means either a real regression (fix the slicer) or an intentional, reviewed label change -- in which case update the baseline EXPLICITLY (never automatically): python -m daedalus.eval --update-baseline
claims.why: The code does not implement CLI argument parsing; it only defines run_gate(). The workflows described are external to this chunk.

claims.text: GUARDRAIL: this gate is ADVISORY ONLY. It is a local developer command plus a unit test (there is no CI in this repo -- verified: no .github/workflows). It must never be wired to block an autonomous action.
claims.why: The code returns 'advisory': True and does not perform any blocking action. The claim about CI and autonomous actions cannot be verified from this chunk alone.

claims.text: ERRORED tasks (see ``run_tier1``) have no recall to compare and are SPLIT by tier, not folded into ``regressions``: * PRIMARY tier  -- FAILS the gate loudly (``errored_primary``, named in the rendered report). A broken primary-corpus task means the gate itself can no longer vouch for that task at all, which must scream exactly like a real recall regression would. * QUARANTINE tier -- reported only (``errored_quarantine``), never fails the gate -- flywheel debris (an unconfirmed minted task whose target moved/vanished) must not be able to block a developer's gate run.
claims.why: In the loop, if 'error' in t, the code checks _is_primary_tier(t['label_tier']) and appends to errored_primary or errored_quarantine respectively. These are separate from regressions. The pass/fail condition is 'passed': len(regressions) == 0 and len(errored_primary) == 0, so primary errors cause failure. Quarantine errors do not affect 'passed'.

claims.text: FOCUS-WITHHELD tasks (the secret floor fail-closed on the task's own focus file -- lane A1) are likewise SPLIT OUT, not folded into ``regressions``: a task that TRANSITIONS to focus-withheld this run has no ``recall`` to compare (fail-closed is not "recall dropped to 0"), so treating it as a regression would be a false alarm on the fence doing its job. Reported in its own ``focus_withheld`` section, regardless of tier, and never fails the gate.
claims.why: In the loop, if t.get('focus_withheld'), the task is appended to focus_withheld list and skipped (continue). It is not included in regressions. The 'passed' condition does not consider focus_withheld, so it never fails the gate.
